transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (CEO), Marco Lee (CTO), Rina Desai (VP Product), Luis Ortega (Head Eng), Hannah Cole (Head of People), plus company-wide attendees

Auto-generated sections: Summary, Topics, Action items (below)

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone, uh, welcome to the Q2 kickoff all-hands. thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week. we'll try to keep this tight, we have a few big updates — Q1 numbers, product roadmap, and some org news.
00:22 Marco: good morning, all. quick note, this call's recorded, and we'll put slides in the #all-hands channel afterwards.
00:30 Sofia: quick show of hands — are we good on the agenda? cool. ok, first up Q1 highlights.
01:02 Sofia: Q1 we finished at $14.2M ARR — net new ARR growth was higher than plan, churn remained low. big shoutout to sales and customer success, we closed two enterprise deals that moved us into new regulated sectors. the dedicated product uptake helped bump committed revenue which is nice for predictability. (applause sounds, some crosstalk)
02:01 Rina: to add, we saw an uptick in POCs for Private deployments, particularly healthcare and finance prospects asking for VPC and on-prem options.
02:27 Luis: yeah, and operationally we've improved P99 latencies by about 12% on the hosted API from the kernel improvements landed in feb. those wins are starting to show in customer benchmarks.
03:00 Sofia: great, let’s dive into product and engineering. Marco, can you lead the runtime/performance update?
03:10 Marco: sure. so brief — our priorities for Q2 are: 1) reduce tail latency further via smarter routing and KV cache improvements, 2) finish the Dedicated autoscaling controls, and 3) roll out the first Private on-prem packaging for regulated customers. we shipped a prototype quantized runtime last month but it needs more validation across workloads — some models show small regressions on a couple of edge prompts.
03:58 Marco: (aside) sorry, uh, mic cut — can everyone still hear me?
04:03 Crowd: yes / yes
04:07 Marco: ok, great. on the routing front, we'll start canarying a cost-aware fallback policy next week. that will let lower-tier traffic automatically route to compatible quantized variants when capacity is constrained. note: this is opt-in for enterprise customers initially.
04:40 Sofia: and that ties to the cost/perf narrative — we want customers to control the latency vs cost tradeoff without guessing. the Optimize toolkit's recommendations will be more prescriptive in Q2.
05:02 Rina: product roadmap: our MLP for this quarter is focused on three things — a streamlined onboarding for POCs (templates, benchmark harness), a formalized model catalog with verified performance profiles, and rollout features for canary/AB with automated rollback. milestone: MLP release candidate targeted for 2026-05-25.
05:35 Attendee 1 (murmur): sounds good
05:42 Rina: we also plan to create a 'redwood-verified' badge for models that pass our perf and quality checks. there's some work with research to define metrics and thresholds.
06:05 Marco: engineering note — we need to run a cross-team benchmark, specifically for Priority customers. action item: Marco and Luis to publish a latency bench and run it against the top 5 enterprise POCs.
06:30 Luis: yep, i'll coordinate with infra to provision Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 for the tests.
06:40 Sofia: perfect. switching to go-to-market — sales, we saw good expansion motions. Hannah, any highlights on hiring and org?
06:55 Hannah: hiring remains top priority. we're opening 24 roles in Q2 across infra, SRE, security, and sales engineering. new comp plan will be in the handbook by Friday. also, we're streamlining interview loops to avoid long delays, pls flag any bottlenecks.
07:20 Hannah: org change — we'll spin a small platform ops team inside infra to focus on Dedicated autoscaling and the Private on-prem installer. Luis will sponsor it.
07:35 Luis: yep, I'll be the exec sponsor. expect a 6-person initial team.
07:45 Audience reaction: (applause emoji in chat)
08:05 Sofia: security/compliance — Rina? or Marco? who has updates on SOC 2 and audit readiness?
08:12 Rina: quick update: we've started a gap assessment for SOC 2 Type II. external auditor selected, the formal audit window is Q3. the security docs (FAQ, evidence collection checklist) will be posted to the partner portal by next week. also, we added KMS/HSM support for Private deployments in the roadmap.
08:45 Marco: technical note — for Private on-prem we need to harden the key management integration, and we need a small set of customer-approved test harnesses so we don't leak any sensitive logs to central telemetry. that will be part of the packaging work.
09:12 Attendee 2: quick question, will there be a dedicated contact for compliance requests?
09:17 Rina: yes, we’ll designate a compliance SME — action: Rina to share contact and the SOC2 timeline. due 2026-04-14.
09:28 Sofia: great. next big topic: customers and POCs. we have three large POCs ramping next quarter with finance and healthcare partners. Marco, what are the performance SLOs we should aim for on those?
09:43 Marco: target P95 latency < 250ms for standard prompts for dedicated pools; P99 less than 500ms if we manage KV cache and batching. that's aggressive but achievable with the new kernel selection and routing heuristics. caveat: long-context workloads will vary, of course.
10:10 Luis: note — for customers requiring on-prem deployment we need to validate network egress restrictions and discrete monitoring endpoints. there are different expectations for logs and telemetry.
10:28 Sofia: ok, community & partnerships — we signed a technical partnership with an inference hardware partner to evaluate new accelerator kernels. expect a joint benchmark in late Q2.
10:42 Rina: also marketing will run a campaign around developer playbooks and quickstarts for POCs. that'll include example configs for Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
11:00 Audience comment: (chat) can we have the playbooks earlier?
11:05 Rina: yes, aim to publish an initial set by 2026-04-21.
11:12 Sofia: org health — quick pulse: our engagement is high, but there are pockets of burnout in infra, we're adding headcount and redistributing project loads. managers, please review your team plans and reach out to People.
11:36 Hannah: we'll do a manager-led check-in next week; also rolling out a flexible time-off policy for Q2 hack days.
11:50 Sofia: finances — we remain capital efficient, runway is healthy post-Series C. we're prioritizing investment in product and security in Q2; marketing spend will be more targeted toward enterprise enablement.
12:10 Audience question: any change to comp or equity?
12:14 Sofia: no company-wide change to equity this quarter; we will do role-level adjustments where needed. HR will follow up.
12:27 Marco: quick technical deep-dive highlight: the quantized runtime we shipped in feb had a few hallucination/regression cases on instruction-following prompts for certain model families. Research and QA are working on prompt-level mitigations and fallback policies. in the short term, we'll gate quantized variants behind canary flags for POCs.
12:55 Attendee 3: are we open-sourcing any parts of the benchmark?
12:59 Marco: we plan to share anonymized benchmark methodologies, not raw customer data. we'll publish a reproducible harness for community use.
13:18 Sofia: growth goals — target for the end of Q2: reach $18M ARR, reduce average latency costs by 8% via Better batching and caching, and onboard 10 new committed Dedicated customers.
13:40 Rina: product asks from customers — they want better model versioning control and easier rollback. that's in our rollout feature set. we'll add an API for pinning and unpinning model versions.
14:00 Luis: ops note — we'll run a maintenance window for the hosted control plane on 2026-04-19. expect minor disruption, we'll post exact times in status.
14:20 Sofia: cool. last section — shoutouts and closing items.
14:28 Sofia: shoutout to the infra crew for the feb patch and to sales for the big enterprise close. also, thanks to the CSMs for the escalations that kept churn low.
14:45 Audience: applause / emojis
15:00 Sofia: recap of next steps — share OKRs, publish the latency benchmark, send SOC2 timeline, and managers schedule team planning. action items and owners will be posted in the #all-hands channel.
15:25 Marco: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an invite for the technical deep-dive next Tuesday for anyone interested.
15:33 Sofia: thanks all. meeting adjourned.
